subject: tsetse fly
title: This Fly Is Pregnant for Days, Then Births a Baby Nearly Her Size

scenes.text: This fly doesn't lay eggs. She gets pregnant.
The tsetse fly of Africa grows one egg at a time. It hatches inside her, in a uterus.
She feeds the larva milk for five or six days. Its proteins work much like those in mammal milk.
She makes more than her own body weight in milk.
Then she gives birth, in under a minute, to a single larva almost as big as she is.
It burrows straight into the ground. She does this about eight times in her life, one giant baby at a time.

description:
The tsetse fly does not lay eggs. A female develops a single egg at a time; it hatches in her uterus and she feeds the larva a milk-like secretion from a milk gland.
After five or six days of milk the larva is fully grown and almost as big as its mother, who gives birth in under a minute; it immediately burrows underground to pupate. A female does this about eight times in her life. Tsetse milk proteins work much like those in mammal milk, according to researchers at UC Davis. Tsetse flies feed only on blood and spread sleeping sickness in sub-Saharan Africa.
Strangest way any animal has babies? Comment below.
first_comment: Sleeping sickness cases fell from about 40,000 in 1998 to under 1,000 in 2018. Which animal has the hardest job as a mother?
